classification.difficultyReason: Identify the ladder as the hypotenuse, calculate the vertical height and convert to centimetres before rounding.

inlines.text: A ladder 4.5 m in length is placed 1.9 m from the base of a vertical wall.
How far does the ladder reach up the wall to the nearest centimetre?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 4 diagram below the prompt on the left.
spec.description: A ladder rises from the lower left to a vertical wall on the right. A separate vertical dimension arrow shows the unknown height.
spec.mathematics: The ladder is the 4.5 m hypotenuse; the horizontal distance is 1.9 m. The wall and ground meet at a right angle. The vertical height is labelled x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied measurements and unknown x are visible; no calculated height is shown.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}a^2+b^2&=h^2\\x^2+1.9^2&=4.5^2\\x^2&=4.5^2-1.9^2\\x^2&=16.64\\x&=\sqrt{16.64}\text{ m}\\x&=100\sqrt{16.64}\text{ cm}\\x&\approx408\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
The ladder reaches 408 cm up the wall, to the nearest centimetre.
